decision: Qualify Qubes resource topologies with per-worker p95 ResourceProbe latency measured from duration-bound calibration evidence.
selectedApproach: carry verified probeLatencyMs into the calibration report, compute per-worker p95, preserve it when applying calibration to a topology, and fail resource-aware topology qualification when the worst worker exceeds an explicit p95 budget

independentReviews.preferredApproach: per-worker p95 latency in the signed/provenance-bound calibration report
independentReviews.reason: a topology with acceptable RAM/CPU can still be operationally unstable if qrexec measurement latency is consistently high; using the same validated probe envelopes prevents a separate uncorrelated timing source

independentReviews.preferredApproach: fail closed when a p95 budget is configured but any worker lacks latency evidence
independentReviews.reason: missing timing evidence must not silently become zero or pass qualification; the duration-bound collector already validates every probe envelope before aggregation

independentReviews.preferredApproach: offline aggregation and evaluator gating with no additional qrexec calls
independentReviews.reason: p95 is derived from probes already executed for resource calibration, so the selected design adds negligible CPU/memory cost and no extra VM, daemon, network listener, or worker mutation

alternatives.approach: keep probe latency as diagnostic-only output
alternatives.rejectedBecause: can select a false-ready topology whose memory and CPU fit but whose qrexec measurement path is unstable

alternatives.approach: run a second dedicated latency benchmark
alternatives.rejectedBecause: adds qrexec traffic and duplicates timing evidence already available around the real ResourceProbe calls

alternatives.approach: gate only on maximum single probe latency
alternatives.rejectedBecause: too sensitive to one scheduling outlier for topology sizing; per-call hard limits remain available while p95 is better for fleet qualification

expectedImpact.correctness: higher; resource-qualified topologies must also satisfy measured transport/probe stability
expectedImpact.robustness: higher; missing p95 evidence fails closed when the budget is enabled
expectedImpact.latency: no additional qrexec round trips; offline percentile computation only
expectedImpact.resourceUse: negligible Map/array and sort overhead over existing calibration samples
expectedImpact.regressionRisk: low; changes are confined to calibration reports, topology resource gating, and tests

qa: duration-bound calibration report exposes probeLatencyP95Ms for every worker
forged or missing per-sample latency evidence remains rejected before aggregation
resource-aware evaluator rejects an otherwise ready topology when one worker p95 exceeds budget
resource-aware evaluator fails closed when p95 budget is configured but worker evidence is missing
legacy resource evaluation remains unchanged when no probe-latency budget is configured
failuresAndLessons: completion-offset validation alone proves probes stayed inside the workload window but does not stop a high-latency Qube from winning fleet selection
measurement evidence should influence the same qualification decision that consumes RAM/vCPU data rather than remain a detached diagnostic
